messages:
elena: noticing a weird mem growth on the sticky cache pool after long-context runs, can anyone eyeball the flamegraphs?

kai: saw that too. looks like repeated small allocations from our compaction path, maybe fragmentation inside page slabs.

priya: aha — reproduction steps? I ran a 40k token convo loop and saw commit rate ~= 2GB / hr on a single worker.

elena: reproduction: run local harness with longctx=40000, batch_size=1, route -> model-a-quant. after ~3k tokens mem rises then plateaus, but after many sessions it climbs again.

kai: posting perf-bot heap diff:
```
perf-bot: heap_before=6.2GB heap_after=8.9GB objects:+12% kv_pages: +230
callstack top: kv_compact -> page_alloc -> memcpy
```

devon: interesting, memcpy hotspots suggest we may be reserializing/rewriting pages when we could coalesce. Any cache-key churn?

priya: yes — key churn is high because we include ephemeral span ids in the cache key. sessions are sticky but sub-requests get new span ids so we miss reuse.

elena: exact problem: our cache key looks like `model|tenant|session|span_v2::<trace>` — span_v2 changes per prompt chunk even when leading tokens identical.

kai: so two things to consider: 1) normalize keys to leading-span fingerprint (hash first N tokens) 2) introduce page-level refcounts to avoid rewrite on transient collisions.

priya: quick experiment: patched key derivation to drop span suffix for keys if session.is_sticky == true. run loop result: mem growth slower, reuse rate +18%, but tail latency increased ~0.6ms on avg.

devon: 0.6ms tradeoff might be OK if cost drops. did you observe any cache poisoning where unrelated prompts get incorrectly reused?

priya: added a lightweight sanity checksum (sha1 of first 32 tokens) in the metadata; only reuse when checksum matches. no poisoning seen in 10k requests test.

elena: also noticed compaction thrash: we compact on every N inserts (N small), which causes page flips. propose making compaction adaptive: if insert rate high, bump threshold and prefer incremental free list repairs.

kai: agree. also we should avoid memcpy when moving cold fragments — use pointer indirection for page headers so we can mark moved segments without copying payload until read.

perf-bot: canary results posted: canary A (key-normalize+checksum) -> hit_rate +21%, mem_growth -35%, p95 latency +0.4ms. canary B (adaptive-compaction) -> mem_growth -42%, p95 latency -0.2ms.

devon: combined change looks promising. action items: (1) pr for key-normalize+checksum (priya) (2) RFC for page indirection (kai) (3) tunes for adaptive compaction threshold (elena).

priya: will open PR with tests and a small feature-flag gated rollout. includes the checksum and a fallback that retains old key behavior if enabled.

kai: i'll sketch the RFC today with diagrams. want to make sure eviction semantics unchanged (refcounts + lazy-copy).

elena: thanks folks. leaving notes here: avoid calling this "prefix reuse" in doc naming — let's call it "leading-span normalization" to reduce confusion with existing heuristics.

devon: thumbs up. will schedule a short sync w/ runtime and sres tomorrow to review canary dashboards. :thumbsup:
